notes: visual-qa 2026-08-02 flags one HIGH issue (twice, at 375 + 393px): the floating glyph-only 'Assistent' button overlapping a mid-agenda row's bottom-right corner (375: the 'National Bank Open presented by Rogers' row; 393: the 13:00 'Tour de France Femmes 2026' row's ⓘ + chevron). At 900px the labelled pill sits cleanly in the empty right margin beside the 640px-capped column (QA: low/no issue).

No PR opened. Independently re-verified the current live state with fresh viewport (non-full-page) screenshots at 375/393/900. The phone-width mitigation is already in place and unchanged since PR #432 / commit 6f3bbd77f (2026-07-31): the button is glyph-only, 44px (HIG minimum touch target), tucked into the extreme corner with a soft (not heavy) shadow; at 900 the pill lives in the empty margin beside the 640px column; the LAST agenda row + footer are never occluded (main.wrap padding-bottom:88px reserves 88px > the FAB's ~58px footprint). Header/tabs/DIREKTE NÅ/day-groups/footer all intact and calm.

This is the same inherent, DESIGN-sanctioned overlap the prior ui-fix runs already minimised. A fixed bottom-trailing button over an edge-to-edge single column unavoidably sits over SOME mid-list row at a given scroll position — DESIGN.md §345–370 (WP-146 variant D, an explicit OWNER decision) sanctions exactly this: the button floats over content and 'Agendaen … scroller rolig UNDER knappen'; only the LAST row is guaranteed clear, and that guarantee holds. It is the iOS 26 floating-button idiom (Foto/Musikk) DESIGN.md references.

Both of visual-qa's proposed remedies are exhausted: bottom-padding is already applied (88px) and cannot fix a position:fixed element's overlap with a MID-list row; shrink-below-a-breakpoint is already done (glyph-only 44px, cannot go below the HIG minimum). The only remaining ways to remove the overlap — dock the control into the flow, use a full-width bottom bar, reserve a permanent right gutter on phones, or hide the FAB — are all explicitly forbidden by DESIGN.md and/or drop the assistant entry on phones (a functional + web-parity regression). Each is an owner-level design decision, outside the ui-fix loop's remit (CLAUDE.md: DESIGN.md is normative, never deviate without explicit owner instruction).

Conservative no-op by design (4th consecutive run to reach this conclusion): shipping another cosmetic tweak on an auto-merging PR would be churn that cannot resolve the inherent overlap and risks a live-site regression. A missing fix beats a regression. Escalation for the owner: to stop this HIGH finding recurring, it needs a DESIGN.md decision on the phone-width assistant-entry pattern — either accept the sanctioned float-over and recalibrate the QA severity to reflect DESIGN.md §345–370, or amend DESIGN.md to reserve a right gutter / change the phone entry pattern. ui-fix cannot act on either without an explicit owner instruction.
